Prevention: Clean farm equipments, after use in infested fields, because seeds and fragmented rhizomes are important in the propagation and spread of couch grass
Use certified clean seed to avoid weed seed introduction through contamination
Practice minimum tillage of infested fields to reduce spread couch grass infestation
While harvesting associated crops like root and tuber crops, ensure that any adhering fragmented rhizomes are removed and destroyed
Monitoring: Perennial, creeping grass with long, slender, branching rhizomes which form a dense mat beneath the soil surface.
Leaves flat, up to 15 cm long and 2-8 mm wide.
Inflorescences branched with 2 to 25 upwardly pointing, 2-11cm long flower heads ('branches')
Check in surrounding areas for presence of this pioneer coloniser
Direct Control: Mechanical tillage with tractor during field preparation helps to expose rhizomes on the soil surface to desiccate in the sun.
Secondary tillage will further expose fragmented rhizomes to desicate in the sun.
When residual plants grow, use forked hoe to remove the rhizomes
Crotolaria, Lab lab, Desmodium can suppress couch grass
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage

Glyphosate (360g per litre of active ingredient per hectare), Glufosinate (500g per litre of active ingredient per hectare), Dicamba (500g per litre of active ingredient per hectare)in non cropped enivironment or before field preparation
